newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Contact Energy posts net NZ$32.6 mln deficit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Contact Energy posts net NZ$32.6 mln deficit.

text.p: State-owned enterprise Contact Energy Ltd on Tuesday reported a net deficit after tax of NZ$32.6 million in the period from its incorporation on November 8, 1995, to September 30, 1996.

Contact said its result was affected by a significant one-off extraordinary adjustment required as part of the establishment of the company. The adjustment resulted in an annualised negative return on average equity of 4.4 percent, compared with the positive return of 6.7 percent anticipated in the 1995/96 statement of corporate intent (SCI).
The annualised return on average equity excluding the effect of the extraordinary adjustment was 7.5 percent.
Contact said its ratio of earnings before interest and tax to average total assets (excluding cash) was 0.3 percent for the period, compared with 8.9 percent in the 1995/96 SCI.
The ratio excluding the effect of the extraordinary adjustment was 10 percent.
The company said it had revalued its assets to economic fair value as at August 31, 1996, in accordance with its Memorandum of Understanding with the government.
As a result, the value of Contact's assets was reduced by NZ$204.3 million.
Contact paid a capital dividend of NZ$150 million during the period.
"The dividend reflects the underlying strength of the statement of financial position despite revaluation and other establishment impacts," the company said.
Gearing rose to 37 percent from 26 percent over the period.

Total revenue for the period was $353.3 million, the largest portion of which was earned through the sale of electricity to Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) under an interim supply contract.
Total costs, excluding asset revaluation and gas write-off items, were $280.2 million.

Contact said capital expenditure of $19 million during the period had been directed at improving the efficiency of existing plant, and foundations had been laid for a strong on-going financial position.
